## Your Turn 02

**New here:** `geom_density()` (smoothed distribution), `fill` + `alpha` (overlap groups, see through).

Draw a **density plot** of `TEMP` to compare the distribution across each `VISIT` using the `vs` dataset.

- Geometry: x-axis = `TEMP`, fill = `VISIT`
- Overlap the curves with `alpha` = 0.4
- Add `theme_minimal()`

```{r}
ggplot(vs, aes(x = ...., fill = ....)) +
  geom_........(alpha = ....) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature Distribution by Visit",
    x = "Temperature",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Your Turn 03

**New here:** `geom_boxplot()` (median/quartiles/outliers), `na.rm = TRUE` (drop missing), `coord_flip()` (swap axes), `scale_fill_brewer()` (palette).

Draw a **box plot** of `SYSBP` across each `VISIT` using the `vs` dataset.

- Geometry: x-axis = `VISIT`, y-axis = `SYSBP`, fill = `VISIT`
- Drop missing values with `na.rm = TRUE`
- Flip horizontally and use palette `"Set2"`

```{r}
ggplot(vs, aes(x = ...., y = ...., fill = ....)) +
  geom_........(na.rm = ....) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "....") +
  ............() +   # flip the chart
  labs(
    title = "Systolic BP Distribution by Visit",
    x = "Visit",
    y = "Systolic Blood Pressure"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Your Turn 04

**New here:** `geom_bar()` (count per category), `labs()` (title/axis/caption), `scale_y_continuous()` (y limits + breaks).

Draw a bar plot to find out the number of subjects in each ARMCD. Use `dm` dataset.

Use following properties:

- Geometry: x-axis = ARMCD and fill = ARMCD
- Title : "Subject Distribution by Treatment Arm",
- X axis : "Treatment Arm",
- Y axis : "Number of Subjects",
- Caption: "Source: Demographics dataset"
- y-axis from 0 to 20, breaks every 5
- Add theme_minimal()

```{r}
ggplot(dm, aes(x = ..., fill = ....)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "...",
    x = "...",
    y = "...",
    caption = "Source: Demographics dataset"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(...., ....),
    breaks = seq(...., ...., by = ....)
  ) +
  ...... # theme_minimal()

```

## Your Turn 06

**New here:** `fill =` second variable, `position = "dodge"` (side-by-side), `scale_fill_manual()` (custom colors).

Draw a **grouped bar plot** of subject counts by `ARMCD`, split by `SEX`, using the `dm` dataset.

- Geometry: x-axis = `ARMCD`, fill = `SEX`
- Place bars side by side with `position = "dodge"`
- Set custom colors: `F` = `"#E69F00"`, `M` = `"#0072B2"`

> Try `position = "fill"` instead to compare proportions rather than counts.

```{r}
ggplot(dm, aes(x = ...., fill = ....)) +
  geom_bar(position = "....") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("F" = "....", "M" = "....")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Subject Count by Treatment Arm and Sex",
    x = "Treatment Arm Code",
    y = "Number of Subjects"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Your Turn 07

**New here:** `fct_infreq()` (order by frequency), `geom_text(stat = "count")` (value labels), `after_stat(count)` (computed count).

Draw a **bar plot** of subject counts by `RACE` using the `dm` dataset, ordered from most to least frequent.

- Reorder bars by frequency with `fct_infreq(RACE)`
- Flip the chart with `coord_flip()`
- Show the count on each bar

```{r}
ggplot(dm, aes(x = ........(RACE))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(
    stat = "....",
    aes(label = after_stat(....)),
    hjust = -0.3
  ) +
  ............() +   # flip the chart
  labs(
    title = "Subject Count by Race",
    x = "Race",
    y = "Number of Subjects"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

## Your Turn 08

**New here:** `geom_point()` (scatter), `alpha` (transparency), `geom_smooth(method = "lm")` (trend line).

Draw a **scatter plot** to explore the relationship between `WEIGHT` and `SYSBP` using the `vs` dataset.

- Geometry: x-axis = `WEIGHT`, y-axis = `SYSBP`, color = `VISIT`
- Make points semi-transparent with `alpha` = 0.6
- Add a straight trend line: `method = "lm"`, `se = FALSE`

```{r}
ggplot(vs, aes(x = ...., y = ....)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = ....), alpha = ...., na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_........(method = "....", se = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Weight vs Systolic Blood Pressure",
    x = "Weight (kg)",
    y = "Systolic Blood Pressure"
  ) +

```
